exposure: Less radical fertility-sparing surgery (simple trachelectomy or large cone biopsy following sentinel lymph node mapping and 'selective parametrectomy') for early-stage cervical cancer
cohort: 91 women (median age 29.1 years, range 21-40) with early-stage cervical cancer (IA1 LVSI positive, IA2, and IB1 <2cm with infiltration less than half of cervical stroma) who underwent less radical fertility-sparing surgery between 1999 and 2018.
finding: Less radical fertility-sparing procedures in women with early-stage cervical cancer resulted in promising pregnancy outcomes, with a pregnancy rate of 85.7% and a delivery rate of 76.2% among those desiring pregnancy.
gest_age: Babies were delivered at various gestational ages: 67.2% at term (39 women), 13 women between 32 and 36+6 weeks, 3 women between 28 and 31+6 weeks, and 3 women between 24 and 27+6 weeks.
